title: UAE Discovery
description: Desert, mountains, sea and seven emirates.

entries.title: The Seven Emirates
entries.summary: The UAE is made of seven emirates.
entries.body: The United Arab Emirates is a country on the Arabian Peninsula. It is made of seven emirates, each with its own ruler and its own character. Abu Dhabi is the largest and Dubai is the busiest.
facts: The seven emirates are Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah.
The UAE has a coastline along the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.
The country joined the United Nations in 1971.

entries.title: Ras Al Khaimah
entries.summary: Ras Al Khaimah has mountains and a long beach.
entries.body: Ras Al Khaimah is the northernmost emirate. It has dramatic mountains that run close to the sea, and beautiful sandy beaches. Red and white fort buildings stand on the hillsides.
facts: The name means 'the top of the head'.
Jais Mountain in Ras Al Khaimah is the highest mountain in the UAE.
It is the only emirate with a coastline on both the Gulf and the Sea of Oman.

entries.title: Dubai
entries.summary: Dubai is a very busy city with the tallest building in the world.
entries.body: Dubai has grown from a small fishing village into one of the world's busiest cities. The Burj Khalifa is the tallest building on Earth. Dubai is also famous for its souks, its beaches and its desert trips.
facts: The Burj Khalifa is more than 800 metres tall.
Dubai has a desert right next to the city.
The Burj Al Arab is shaped like a sailing boat.

entries.title: The Rub' al Khali
entries.summary: The Empty Quarter is the biggest desert in the Arab peninsula.
entries.body: The Rub' al Khali means 'the empty quarter'. It is a huge sea of sand that covers the south of the Arabian Peninsula. Bedouin families have lived there for hundreds of years, travelling with their camels.
facts: The dunes here can be more than 100 metres tall.
The dunes shift a little every year with the wind.
Camels are still the best way to travel across it.

entries.title: The Date Palm
entries.summary: The date palm is a national treasure of the UAE.
entries.body: Date palms grow in the oases where water comes up from under the ground. Dates have been eaten in this region for thousands of years and they are still an important crop today. A single palm can produce hundreds of kilos of dates.
facts: A date palm can live for more than 100 years.
Oases are green spots in the middle of the desert.
Dates are a great source of energy for people and animals.

entries.title: Falcons
entries.summary: Falcons have been part of life in the UAE for thousands of years.
entries.body: Falcons are fast hunting birds. People in the region have trained them to hunt for thousands of years, and falconry is part of the country's heritage. Falconry was also listed by UNESCO as part of the UAE's world heritage.
facts: Falcons can dive at more than 300 kilometres an hour.
Their sharp eyesight helps them spot prey from high up.
The UAE's national bird is the falcon.
